answer: Every close the protocol publishes one settlement pool for the epoch and divides it equally among the heads whose answers its jury passed, so a head's own share is that pool divided by the number of heads that cleared it. One honest head takes the cedar's full height; a farm of a thousand heads splits the same tree into a thousand threads, and each extra head must post the same capital as the rest just to be worth the same. The divisor is set by the crowd's own outcome at the close and cannot be pre-split, so the summit payout of a cloned crowd is thin by construction.
